content:
Hi everyone! I’m a mathematics student and I recently started using Lean while trying to formalize a new result I found in combinatorics.
While learning Lean I came across this community, and I really liked the idea behind the collaborative development of Lean and its libraries. So I thought I’d try to get involved and contribute something in combinatorics as well.
I’m still pretty new to Lean, so I’d ideally like to start with something small and manageable. Are there any open combinatorics topics that could be a good first project?
Also, if I manage to finish something useful, where would be the right place to contribute it / how does that usually work?
Thanks a lot, and great to meet you all!
Hello! For the last question, you can look at the contribution guide
Welcome! What topics are you interested in?
Thank you both for your replies :) I’m mostly interested in finite combinatorics and graph theory, with some interest in number theory too, but I’m quite open
The only thing I know about graph theory is that Mathlib needs more reviewers in that area :smile:

Filippo Cavallari said:

graph theory

Great! There are loads of stuff missing, but I think finding something to motivate you is the key :)
You could try:

  • In a preconnected graph, any two longest paths intersect
  • preconnected ↔ any new edge creates a cycle that uses that edge
  • p.IsPath ↔ p.toSubgraph.coe.IsAcyclic
  • There exists a path with length equal to G.ediam / G.radius / G.eccent v
  • Find the spectra of known graphs (completeGraph / pathGraph / starGraph)
  • (cycleGraph <| 2 * k + 3)ᶜ.cliqueNum = k
  • Define the Rado graph / Petersen graph and prove properties about it
  • Calculating the diameter of trees: G.IsTree → G.eccent u = G.edist u v → G.ediam = G.eccent v
  • docs#SimpleGraph.cycleGraph.cycle is an Eulerian walk (docs#SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian)
  • In a preconnected graph with max-degree ≤ 2, any Eulerian walk is Hamiltonian

etc. Anything wink at you so far? Or do you perhaps have any theorems you know that you're wondering whether they exist? These are just stuff I think are missing, but if you play around with the API you'll probably find other missing lemmas pretty quick

Thanks! That’s really helpful. The first two caught my attention the most: they both sound interesting, and they also seem somewhat related, so I would be happy to start with one of those.
I’ll take a deeper look at the API, but since I don’t have another specific theorem in mind at the moment, I think one of these would be a good place to start.
